props.title: Who's the Man?
props.initialSlug: Two barbers become unlikely NYPD cops in Harlem

sections.content: Who's the Man (1993)? represents a fascinating intersection of hip-hop culture and police comedy during rap's golden age. Directed by Ted Demme, who later helmed Beautiful Girls (1996) and Blow (2001), this film stars Doctor Dré and Ed Lover from "Yo! MTV Raps" as two bumbling barbers-turned-police officers. The film captures a specific moment when hip-hop was transitioning from underground phenomenon to mainstream cultural force, similar to how House Party (1990) and New Jack City (1991) documented different aspects of early 90s Black urban culture.

sections.content: The film's greatest strength lies in its impressive roster of hip-hop cameos, featuring icons like Ice-T, Run-DMC, Queen Latifah, and Busta Rhymes. This approach of incorporating multiple rap artists follows a tradition started by Wild Style (1983) and Krush Groove (1985), films that documented hip-hop culture while it was still emerging. The comedy style blends slapstick with social commentary, similar to what I'm Gonna Git You Sucka (1988) achieved with its blaxploitation parody.

While Who's the Man? may not reach the satirical heights of Fear of a Black Hat (1993) or the cultural impact of Boyz n the Hood (1991), it serves as a valuable time capsule of early 90s hip-hop culture. The film's mix of comedy and community policing themes predates later works like Training Day (2001) and Brooklyn's Finest (2009), though with a much lighter touch. SUBHEAD: Hip-Hop Cinema Evolution

sections.content: The film sits at an interesting crossroads between pure hip-hop celebration films like Beat Street (1984) and more serious urban dramas that would follow. Its comedy-first approach, while dated in some aspects, helped pave the way for later hip-hop comedies like Friday (1995) and Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood (1996), which would similarly blend neighborhood stories with broader comedy.
